sanskrit: na tv enaṃ pīḍayām āsa balena balavattaraḥ tato hi jīvitaṃ tasya na vyanīnaśad acyutaḥ
english: Yet the Infallible One, though far mightier in strength, did not crush him utterly; and thus Acyuta did not cause the bird's life to perish.

sanskrit: vipakṣaḥ srastakāyaś ca vicetā vihvalaḥ khagaḥ mumoca patrāṇi tadā gurubhāraprapīḍitaḥ
english: With wings pinioned, his body drooping, senses scattered, and mind reeling, the bird let fall his feathers, overwhelmed by that immense burden.

sanskrit: sa viṣṇuṃ śirasā pakṣī praṇamya vinatāsutaḥ vicetā vihvalo dīnaḥ kiṃ cid vacanam abravīt
english: Then the bird, son of Vinatā, bowed his head before Viṣṇu and, bewildered, dazed, and pitiful, spoke these words.

sanskrit: bhagavaṃl lokasārasya sadṛśena vapuṣmatā bhujena svairamuktena niṣpiṣṭo 'smi mahītale
english: "O Lord, with an arm worthy of one who is the essence of all worlds—an arm released at will—I have been ground into the earth."

sanskrit: kṣantum arhasi me deva vihvalasyālpacetasaḥ baladāhavidagdhasya pakṣiṇo dhvajavāsinaḥ
english: "Deign to forgive me, O God—a bird confused and feeble-minded, scorched by the fire of arrogance, who dwells upon your banner."

sanskrit: na vijñātaṃ balaṃ deva mayā te paramaṃ vibho tena manyāmy ahaṃ vīryam ātmano 'sadṛśaṃ paraiḥ
english: "I did not know your supreme might, O Lord, O Pervader—therefore I thought my own prowess unmatched by others."

sanskrit: tataś cakre sa bhagavān prasādaṃ vai garutmataḥ maivaṃ bhūya iti snehāt tadā cainam uvāca ha
english: Then the Blessed Lord showed grace to Garuṭmān; out of affection he said to him, "Be not thus again."

sanskrit: tathā tvam api gāndhāre yāvat pāṇḍusutān raṇe nāsādayasi tān vīrāṃs tāvaj jīvasi putraka
english: "Likewise you, O son of Gāndhāra—as long as you do not encounter those heroic sons of Pāṇḍu in battle, so long shall you live, my child."

sanskrit: bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ śreṣṭho vāyuputro mahābalaḥ dhanaṃjayaś cendrasuto na hanyātāṃ tu kaṃ raṇe
english: "Bhīma, son of Vāyu, the foremost of warriors, of immense strength, and Dhanaṃjaya, son of Indra—whom could those two not slay in battle?"

sanskrit: viṣṇur vāyuś ca śakraś ca dharmas tau cāśvināv ubhau ete devās tvayā kena hetunā śakyam īkṣitum
english: "Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Śakra, Dharma, and the two Aśvins—by what means could you stand to face these gods?"

sanskrit: tad alaṃ te virodhena śamaṃ gaccha nṛpātmaja vāsudevena tīrthena kulaṃ rakṣitum arhasi
english: "Therefore, enough of this enmity—seek peace, O son of a king; by the sacred ford of Vāsudeva you ought to preserve your lineage."

sanskrit: pratyakṣo hy asya sarvasya nārado 'yaṃ mahātapāḥ māhātmyaṃ yat tadā viṣṇor yo 'yaṃ cakragadādharaḥ
english: "Indeed, Nārada of great austerity is a direct witness to all of this—to the majesty of that Viṣṇu who bears the discus and mace."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca duryodhanas tu tac chrutvā niḥśvasan bhṛkuṭīmukhaḥ rādheyam abhisaṃprekṣya jahāsa svanavat tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But Duryodhana, having heard all this, only heaved a sigh with furrowed brow; he glanced at Rādheya and then laughed aloud.

sanskrit: kadarthīkṛtya tad vākyam ṛṣeḥ kaṇvasya durmatiḥ ūruṃ gajakarākāraṃ tāḍayann idam abravīt
english: The evil-minded one, having dismissed the words of the seer Kaṇva as worthless, slapped his thigh—thick as an elephant's trunk—and said this:

sanskrit: yathaiveśvarasṛṣṭo 'smi yad bhāvi yā ca me gatiḥ tathā maharṣe vartāmi kiṃ pralāpaḥ kariṣyati
english: "As I was created by the Lord, as whatever is destined to happen will happen, and as my course is fixed—so I conduct myself, O great seer. What will this babbling accomplish?"

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca anarthe jātanirbandhaṃ parārthe lobhamohitam anāryakeṣv abhirataṃ maraṇe kṛtaniścayam
english: Janamejaya said: He who is fixedly bent upon ruin, who is blinded by greed in the affairs of others, who delights in ignoble acts, who has resolved on destruction—

sanskrit: jñātīnāṃ duḥkhakartāraṃ bandhūnāṃ śokavardhanam suhṛdāṃ kleśadātāraṃ dviṣatāṃ harṣavardhanam
english: —who is a source of pain to his kinsmen, who increases the grief of relatives, who gives sorrow to friends and joy to enemies—

sanskrit: kathaṃ nainaṃ vimārgasthaṃ vārayantīha bāndhavāḥ sauhṛdād vā suhṛtsnigdho bhagavān vā pitāmahaḥ
english: —how is it that his kinsmen do not restrain this one gone astray? Or out of affection a devoted friend, or the venerable Pitāmaha himself?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uktaṃ bhagavatā vākyam uktaṃ bhīṣmeṇa yat kṣamam uktaṃ bahuvidhaṃ caiva nāradenāpi tac chṛṇu
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: What was fitting was spoken by the Blessed One; what was fitting was spoken by Bhīṣma; and what was manifold in kind was spoken also by Nārada—hear that.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca durlabho vai suhṛc chrotā durlabhaś ca hitaḥ suhṛt tiṣṭhate hi suhṛd yatra na bandhus tatra tiṣṭhati
english: Nārada said: Rare indeed is the friend who truly listens, and rare the friend who truly means well. A friend stands where a kinsman does not stand.

sanskrit: śrotavyam api paśyāmi suhṛdāṃ kurunandana na kartavyaś ca nirbandho nirbandho hi sudāruṇaḥ
english: I see that the words of friends ought to be heeded, O joy of the Kurus; and one should not cling stubbornly—for stubborn insistence is utterly terrible.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yathā nirbandhataḥ prāpto gālavena parājayaḥ
english: On this point, too, they cite this ancient tale—how Gālava came to grief through stubborn insistence.

sanskrit: viśvāmitraṃ tapasyantaṃ dharmo jijñāsayā purā abhyagacchat svayaṃ bhūtvā vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Long ago, Dharma, wishing to test Viśvāmitra as he performed austerities, approached him himself, taking the form of the venerable seer Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: saptarṣīṇām anyatamaṃ veṣam āsthāya bhārata bubhukṣuḥ kṣudhito rājann āśramaṃ kauśikasya ha
english: Assuming the guise of one of the seven sages, O Bhārata, O king, hungry and craving food, he came to the hermitage of Kauśika.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'tha saṃbhrāntaḥ śrapayām āsa vai carum paramānnasya yatnena na ca sa pratyapālayat
english: Viśvāmitra, greatly agitated, set about cooking a dish of the finest food with great effort—but that guest did not wait for it.

sanskrit: annaṃ tena yadā bhuktam anyair dattaṃ tapasvibhiḥ atha gṛhyānnam atyuṣṭhaṃ viśvāmitro 'bhyupāgamat
english: When the food he had taken was eaten—given to him by other ascetics—Viśvāmitra came forward bearing the food that was still very hot.

sanskrit: bhuktaṃ me tiṣṭha tāvat tvam ity uktvā bhagavān yayau viśvāmitras tato rājan sthita eva mahādyutiḥ
english: "Wait for me—I have eaten," said the Blessed One, and departed; and Viśvāmitra, the greatly resplendent, stood there and waited, O king.

sanskrit: bhaktaṃ pragṛhya mūrdhnā tad bāhubhyāṃ pārśvato 'gamat sthitaḥ sthāṇur ivābhyāśe niśceṣṭo mārutāśanaḥ
english: Holding that food reverently on his head, he stood to one side with his arms; motionless as a pillar nearby, he subsisted on air alone.

sanskrit: tasya śuśrūṣaṇe yatnam akarod gālavo muniḥ gauravād bahumānāc ca hārdena priyakāmyayā
english: The sage Gālava made every effort to serve him—out of reverence, deep respect, heartfelt devotion, and desire to please.

sanskrit: atha varṣaśate pūrṇe dharmaḥ punar upāgamat vāsiṣṭhaṃ veṣam āsthāya kauśikaṃ bhojanepsayā
english: Then, when a full hundred years had passed, Dharma came again, assuming the form of Vasiṣṭha, desiring food from Kauśika.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā śirasā bhaktaṃ dhriyamāṇaṃ maharṣiṇā tiṣṭhatā vāyubhakṣeṇa viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā
english: He saw the food being held reverently on the head of that great seer—the wise Viśvāmitra, who had stood there subsisting on air alone.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tato dharmas tathaivoṣṇaṃ tathā navam bhuktvā prīto 'smi viprarṣe tam uktvā sa munir gataḥ
english: Then Dharma accepted the food—still hot, still fresh—and having eaten it, said to him "I am pleased, O seer among brahmin sages," and that sage departed.

sanskrit: kṣatrabhāvād apagato brāhmaṇatvam upāgataḥ dharmasya vacanāt prīto viśvāmitras tadābhavat
english: Having moved beyond the nature of a kṣatriya and attained brahmanhood, Viśvāmitra was then filled with joy at Dharma's words.

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu śiṣyasya gālavasya tapasvinaḥ śuśrūṣayā ca bhaktyā ca prītimān ity uvāca tam anujñāto mayā vatsa yatheṣṭaṃ gaccha gālava
english: And Viśvāmitra, pleased by the service and devotion of his ascetic disciple Gālava, said to him: "You have my leave, my child—go wherever you wish, Gālava."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ gālavo munisattamam prīto madhurayā vācā viśvāmitraṃ mahādyutim
english: Addressed thus, Gālava spoke these words in reply to that best of sages, to the resplendent Viśvāmitra, with a sweet and joyful voice:

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāṃ kāṃ prayacchāmi bhavate gurukarmaṇi dakṣiṇābhir upetaṃ hi karma sidhyati mānavam
english: "What fee shall I give you for this work of a guru? For a human undertaking succeeds only when accompanied by the proper gift."

sanskrit: dakṣiṇānāṃ hi sṛṣṭānām apavargeṇa bhujyate svarge kratuphalaṃ sadbhir dakṣiṇā śāntir ucyate kim āharāmi gurvarthaṃ bravītu bhagavān iti
english: "For it is taught that the fruit of a sacrifice in heaven is enjoyed only through the completion of gifts; by the good, the fee is called peace itself. What shall I bring for my teacher's sake? Let the Blessed One say."

sanskrit: jānamānas tu bhagavāñ jitaḥ śuśrūṣaṇena ca viśvāmitras tam asakṛd gaccha gacchety acodayat
english: But the Blessed One, though knowing, conquered by Gālava's service, urged him again and again: "Go, go."

sanskrit: asakṛd gaccha gaccheti viśvāmitreṇa bhāṣitaḥ kiṃ dadānīti bahuśo gālavaḥ pratyabhāṣata
english: Being told again and again "go, go" by Viśvāmitra, Gālava replied over and over: "What shall I give?"

sanskrit: nirbandhatas tu bahuśo gālavasya tapasvinaḥ kiṃ cid āgatasaṃrambho viśvāmitro 'bravīd idam
english: But pressed again and again by the ascetic Gālava's insistence, Viśvāmitra, somewhat roused to irritation, said this:

sanskrit: ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ śatāny aṣṭau dadasva me hayānāṃ candraśubhrāṇāṃ gaccha gālava māciram
english: "Give me eight hundred horses—white as the moon, each with one black ear—and go, Gālava, delay no more."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca evam uktas tadā tena viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā nāste na śete nāhāraṃ kurute gālavas tadā
english: Nārada said: Thus addressed by the wise Viśvāmitra, Gālava neither sat nor lay down nor took food after that.

sanskrit: tvagasthibhūto hariṇaś cintāśokaparāyaṇaḥ śocamāno 'timātraṃ sa dahyamānaś ca manyunā
english: Reduced to skin and bones like a deer, wholly given over to worry and grief, lamenting beyond measure, and burning with anguish,

sanskrit: kutaḥ puṣṭāni mitrāṇi kuto 'rthāḥ saṃcayaḥ kutaḥ hayānāṃ candraśubhrāṇāṃ śatāny aṣṭau kuto mama
english: "Where are wealthy friends? Where is accumulated wealth? Where, for me, are eight hundred horses white as the moon?"

sanskrit: kuto me bhojanaśraddhā sukhaśraddhā kutaś ca me śraddhā me jīvitasyāpi chinnā kiṃ jīvitena me
english: "Where is my desire for food? Where my desire for happiness? My very will to live is severed. What use is life to me?"

sanskrit: ahaṃ pāraṃ samudrasya pṛthivyā vā paraṃ parāt gatvātmānaṃ vimuñcāmi kiṃ phalaṃ jīvitena me
english: "I shall go to the far shore of the ocean, or to what lies beyond the farthest edge of the earth, and abandon myself there. What fruit is there in living?"

sanskrit: adhanasyākṛtārthasya tyaktasya vividhaiḥ phalaiḥ ṛṇaṃ dhārayamāṇasya kutaḥ sukham anīhayā
english: "For one who is poor, whose purpose is unfulfilled, who has been abandoned by every kind of fruit, who carries a debt—where is happiness in listlessness?"

sanskrit: suhṛdāṃ hi dhanaṃ bhuktvā kṛtvā praṇayam īpsitam pratikartum aśaktasya jīvitān maraṇaṃ varam
english: "For one who has enjoyed the wealth of friends, who has received their cherished affection, and who is unable to repay them—death is better than life."

sanskrit: pratiśrutya kariṣyeti kartavyaṃ tad akurvataḥ mithyāvacanadagdhasya iṣṭāpūrtaṃ praṇaśyati
english: "For one who has promised 'I will do it' and does not do what must be done—burned by the fire of false speech—the merit of sacrifices and charitable works is destroyed."

sanskrit: na rūpam anṛtasyāsti nānṛtasyāsti saṃtatiḥ nānṛtasyādhipatyaṃ ca kuta eva gatiḥ śubhā
english: "Untruth has no form; untruth has no progeny; untruth has no sovereignty—how then could it have an auspicious end?"

sanskrit: kutaḥ kṛtaghnasya yaśaḥ kutaḥ sthānaṃ kutaḥ sukham aśraddheyaḥ kṛtaghno hi kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ
english: "Where is the glory of the ungrateful? Where his station? Where his happiness? The ungrateful cannot be trusted—and for ingratitude there is no atonement."

sanskrit: na jīvaty adhanaḥ pāpaḥ kutaḥ pāpasya tantraṇam pāpo dhruvam avāpnoti vināśaṃ nāśayan kṛtam
english: "The sinful man without wealth does not truly live. Where is the governance of sin? The sinful one surely reaches destruction, destroying what was done for him."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ pāpaḥ kṛtaghnaś ca kṛpaṇaś cānṛto 'pi ca guror yaḥ kṛtakāryaḥ saṃs tat karomi na bhāṣitam so 'haṃ prāṇān vimokṣyāmi kṛtvā yatnam anuttamam
english: "I am that sinful, ungrateful, wretched, and untruthful one who, though benefited by my teacher, does not do what I promised. I shall release my vital breaths after making one final supreme effort."

sanskrit: arthanā na mayā kā cit kṛtapūrvā divaukasām mānayanti ca māṃ sarve tridaśā yajñasaṃstare
english: "I have never before petitioned the gods; and yet all the thirty gods honor me in the midst of sacrificial assemblies."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu vibudhaśreṣṭhaṃ devaṃ tribhuvaneśvaram viṣṇuṃ gacchāmy ahaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ gatiṃ gatimatāṃ varam
english: "I shall go to Viṣṇu—the foremost of the wise, the god who is lord of the three worlds, to Kṛṣṇa, the best refuge for those who seek refuge."

sanskrit: bhogā yasmāt pratiṣṭhante vyāpya sarvān surāsurān prayato draṣṭum icchāmi mahāyoginam avyayam
english: "He from whom all enjoyments are established, pervading all gods and asuras—I wish to behold, with a pure heart, that great Yogin, the imperishable."

sanskrit: evam ukte sakhā tasya garuḍo vinatātmajaḥ darśayām āsa taṃ prāha saṃhṛṣṭaḥ priyakāmyayā
english: When he had spoken thus, his friend Garuḍa, the son of Vinatā, appeared before him and spoke joyfully, wishing to please him:

sanskrit: suhṛd bhavān mama mataḥ suhṛdāṃ ca mataḥ suhṛt īpsitenābhilāṣeṇa yoktavyo vibhave sati
english: "You are regarded as my friend and as a friend among friends; a friend with resources should be engaged with the cherished desire of a friend."

sanskrit: vibhavaś cāsti me vipra vāsavāvarajo dvija pūrvam uktas tvadarthaṃ ca kṛtaḥ kāmaś ca tena me
english: "I have resources, O brahmin—the younger brother of Vāsava has previously been spoken to on your behalf, and he has granted my wish for your sake."

sanskrit: sa bhavān etu gacchāva nayiṣye tvāṃ yathāsukham deśaṃ pāraṃ pṛthivyā vā gaccha gālava māciram
english: "So come, let us go—I will carry you comfortably to any place, or even to the far shore of the earth. Go, Gālava, delay no more."

sanskrit: suparṇa uvāca anuśiṣṭo 'smi devena gālavājñātayoninā brūhi kām anusaṃyāmi draṣṭuṃ prathamato diśam
english: Suparṇa said: I have been instructed by the Lord—by him who knows all origins and causes, O Gālava. Tell me: which direction shall I follow to visit first?

sanskrit: pūrvāṃ vā dakṣiṇāṃ vāham atha vā paścimāṃ diśam uttarāṃ vā dvijaśreṣṭha kuto gacchāmi gālava
english: "Shall I go east, south, west, or north, O best of twice-born? Where shall I go, O Gālava?"

sanskrit: yasyām udayate pūrvaṃ sarvalokaprabhāvanaḥ savitā yatra saṃdhyāyāṃ sādhyānāṃ vartate tapaḥ
english: "In that direction where the Sun who illumines all worlds first rises, where at twilight the Sādhyas perform their austerities—

sanskrit: yasyāṃ pūrvaṃ matir jātā yayā vyāptam idaṃ jagat cakṣuṣī yatra dharmasya yatra caiṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: "—in which direction was the primordial mind first born, by which this world is pervaded; where are the two eyes of Dharma, where he himself is established—

sanskrit: hutaṃ yatomukhair havyaṃ sarpate sarvatodiśam etad dvāraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha divasasya tathādhvanaḥ
english: "—from whose mouths the oblation offered glides in every direction: this is the door, O best of twice-born, of the day and of the path itself—

sanskrit: yatra pūrvaṃ prasūtā vai dākṣāyaṇyaḥ prajāḥ striyaḥ yasyāṃ diśi pravṛddhāś ca kaśyapasyātmasaṃbhavāḥ
english: "—where the daughters of Dakṣa and their offspring were first born, where the sons born of Kaśyapa's own self grew mighty—

sanskrit: yatomūlā surāṇāṃ śrīr yatra śakro 'bhyaṣicyata surarājyena viprarṣe devaiś cātra tapaś citam
english: "—from where the glory of the gods has its root, where Śakra was consecrated to the sovereignty of the gods, O seer among brahmins, and where austerities were accumulated by the gods—

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād brahman pūrvety eṣā dig ucyate yasmāt pūrvatare kāle pūrvam eṣāvṛtā suraiḥ
english: "—for this reason, O brahmin, this direction is called 'East,' because in a more ancient time the gods first frequented it.

sanskrit: ata eva ca pūrveṣāṃ pūrvām āśām avekṣatām pūrvakāryāṇi kāryāṇi daivāni sukham īpsatā
english: "And for this very reason, for those of ancient lineage who look toward the eastern quarter, the primary works to be done are the divine works—by one who desires happiness."

sanskrit: atra vedāñ jagau pūrvaṃ bhagavāṃl lokabhāvanaḥ atraivoktā savitrāsīt sāvitrī brahmavādiṣu
english: "Here the Lord, the sustainer of worlds, first chanted the Vedas; here the Sāvitrī was first spoken by Savitṛ among those who discourse on Brahman."

sanskrit: atra dattāni sūryeṇa yajūṃṣi dvijasattama atra labdhavaraiḥ somaḥ suraiḥ kratuṣu pīyate
english: "Here the Yajus were given by the Sun, O best of twice-born; here, by the gods who have obtained their boons, Soma is drunk at sacrifices."

sanskrit: atra tṛptā hutavahāḥ svāṃ yonim upabhuñjate atra pātālam āśritya varuṇaḥ śriyam āpa ca
english: "Here the fire-gods, satisfied, enjoy their own source; here, resorting to the netherworld Pātāla, Varuṇa attained his sovereignty."

sanskrit: atra pūrvaṃ vasiṣṭhasya paurāṇasya dvijarṣabha sūtiś caiva pratiṣṭhā ca nidhanaṃ ca prakāśate
english: "Here, O best of twice-born seers, were made manifest the ancient Vasiṣṭha's birth, his establishment, and his dissolution."

sanskrit: oṃkārasyātra jāyante sūtayo daśatīr daśa pibanti munayo yatra havirdhāne sma somapāḥ
english: "Here a hundred decades of Oṃkāra's revelations are born; here the sages, drinkers of Soma, drink at the altar of the oblation shed."

sanskrit: prokṣitā yatra bahavo varāhādyā mṛgā vane śakreṇa yatra bhāgārthe daivateṣu prakalpitāḥ
english: "Here many animals in the forest—boars and others—were consecrated and assigned by Śakra to the gods as their share of the sacrifice."

sanskrit: atrāhitāḥ kṛtaghnāś ca mānuṣāś cāsurāś ca ye udayaṃs tān hi sarvān vai krodhād dhanti vibhāvasuḥ
english: "Here the impure and ungrateful ones—whether human or demonic—who arise are slain in wrath by the Blazing One himself."

sanskrit: etad dvāraṃ trilokasya svargasya ca sukhasya ca eṣa pūrvo diśābhāgo viśāvainaṃ yadīcchasi
english: "This is the door of the three worlds, of heaven, and of happiness. This is the eastern quarter—enter it if you wish."

sanskrit: priyaṃ kāryaṃ hi me tasya yasyāsmi vacane sthitaḥ brūhi gālava yāsyāmi śṛṇu cāpy aparāṃ diśam
english: "It is dear to me to serve him in whose word I abide. Say, Gālava, I will go—but also listen to the next direction."

sanskrit: suparṇa uvāca iyaṃ vivasvatā pūrvaṃ śrautena vidhinā kila gurave dakṣiṇā dattā dakṣiṇety ucyate 'tha dik
english: Suparṇa said: This is the direction in which, it is said, Vivasvān formerly gave the sacrificial fee to his teacher according to Vedic rite—therefore it is called the South.

sanskrit: atra lokatrayasyāsya pitṛpakṣaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ atroṣmapānāṃ devānāṃ nivāsaḥ śrūyate dvija
english: "Here the ancestral side of all these three worlds is established; here, it is heard, is the dwelling of the gods who drink the warm oblation, O twice-born."
